usageNotes: Use this to read the full configuration of a specific LXC container, including CPU, memory, network interfaces, mount points, and rootfs details. By default the API returns pending (not-yet-applied) values; pass `current: true` to get the live running configuration. To inspect a historical state, provide a `snapshot` name instead — `current` and `snapshot` are mutually exclusive.

examples.summary: Fetch the current running config for LXC container 101 on node pve1

tips: The `digest` field in the response is a SHA1 of the config file — pass it back in write operations to guard against concurrent modifications.
A `lock` field in the response indicates an in-progress operation (backup, migrate, snapshot, etc.); writes will be rejected until the lock clears.
Network interfaces are returned as `net0`, `net1`, ... and mount points as `mp0`, `mp1`, ... — enumerate these keys in your client since the count varies per container.
If `unprivileged` is false, the container runs as root on the host; treat privileged containers with extra care when reading security-sensitive config.
Omitting both `current` and `snapshot` returns pending config, which may differ from what is actually running if a config change has not been applied yet.
